past_kind: 2025 provisional outturn; not final audited spending

sectors.intro: Social protection connects pension payments, supports during illness or unemployment, family payments and other income supports. It is one of Ireland's largest spending sectors because cash transfers reach households at different stages of life.
sectors.interpretation: A large figure here does not mean everyone receives an equal cash transfer. Eligibility and payment rates differ, and some services are administered rather than paid directly to households.
sectors.context: The useful distinction is between pensions, payments for working-age people, supports for families and administrative services. The programme-level split has to be taken from departmental Estimates before assigning euro amounts to any of these headings.
questions: Does my PRSI pay for my own State Pension?
PRSI contributes to social insurance funding, but you do not hold a personal fund representing the PRSI you paid. State Pension eligibility depends on contribution records and the rules in force.
Can I treat all social protection spending as welfare for unemployed people?
No. The sector also includes pensions, disability and illness supports, family payments and other programmes.
Does Child Benefit count as a service or a cash payment?
Child Benefit is a cash transfer. It should be reported separately from the estimated cost of public services used.

sectors.intro: Health expenditure supports the public system's capacity to deliver hospital treatment, primary care, community services, medicines and other services. It includes much more than the cost of visits a household happens to make this year.
sectors.interpretation: National health expenditure cannot be divided by population and described as the actual medical benefit received by each person. Shared capacity, access rules and individual needs all matter.
sectors.context: An authoritative deeper split would distinguish hospital services, primary and community care, mental health, care for older people and medicines. Those programme-level financial amounts are not implied by the sector total.
questions: Is €27.4bn what the HSE spent in 2026?
It is the published 2026 sector estimate in this snapshot, not a confirmed year-end HSE outturn. The sector and the HSE are not necessarily identical accounting boundaries.
Do people with private health insurance receive no health benefit?
No. Emergency capacity, public health functions and many services remain relevant; private insurance does not remove the public system from an individual's life.
Why can health spending rise without waiting lists falling?
Costs, population needs, staffing, capacity and service performance can change separately. An expenditure increase is not itself an outcome measure.

sectors.intro: Education spending includes primary and post-primary education, teaching, school supports, school buildings and services for pupils with additional needs. The sector's financial scope should not be confused with the entire higher-education system.
sectors.interpretation: An education figure is a budget allocation, not a cash payment to a parent. Per-pupil costs are a separate analysis requiring consistent enrolment and expenditure definitions.
sectors.context: Further and higher education sits within a separate department after the 2020 transfer of functions, so readers should not assume the headline school-sector amount includes every university and apprenticeship programme.
questions: Does the education sector total include university spending?
Not all of it. Further and higher education was transferred to a distinct department in 2020; check programme boundaries when comparing years.
Can school spending be calculated for an individual child?
Average expenditure per pupil may be estimated with suitable official figures, but it is not the same as the services that child actually received.
Are school building projects included in the total?
Capital expenditure can be included in departmental estimates, but named projects need separate verified allocations and should not be counted twice.

sectors.intro: Housing expenditure is connected with the supply of social and affordable housing, support for eligible renters, homelessness responses and related public programmes. The headline sector also interacts with local government responsibilities.
sectors.interpretation: Housing funding, new-home completions and tenancy supports are different measurements. Funding commitments cannot simply be read as the number of new homes delivered.
sectors.context: Housing was previously presented within Additional Departments before 2020 on the official site. A ten-year trend that ignores this classification change would be misleading.
questions: Does the housing total mean that amount was spent building new houses?
No. A broad housing allocation is not identical to direct construction spending. It can also include rental supports and other programmes.
Can spending explain the number of completed social homes?
Only when the underlying expenditure scope and completion measure are matched; acquisition, construction, leasing and supports differ.
Can pre-2020 numbers be compared directly?
Use caution. The source amalgamated housing spending into Additional Departments before 2020.

sectors.intro: Justice spending covers policing, courts, prisons and other parts of the justice system. Some services are preventative or protective rather than a benefit that a household actively claims.
sectors.interpretation: The difference between this broad sector estimate and a single agency's operational budget matters. Costs at department, programme and agency level must be mapped before making fine-grained claims.
sectors.context: A rise or fall in the published total does not by itself measure crime, safety or the quality of public services. Staffing, service volumes and outcomes need separate official evidence.
questions: Is justice spending just Garda salaries?
No. Policing is one element alongside courts, prisons, administration and associated services.
Does lower expenditure mean less safety?
Not necessarily. Outcomes depend on service demand, delivery and capacity, not solely the budget amount.
Where can I find particular agency payments?
Agency accounts, departmental Estimates, procurement records and audit reports can provide additional detail when published.

sectors.intro: Transport expenditure helps fund public transport services, major infrastructure, roads and active travel. New construction, ongoing maintenance and subsidised services are different spending types.
sectors.interpretation: A project announcement is not the same as expenditure actually incurred. For major transport schemes, follow estimates, approvals, contracts and delivery updates separately.
sectors.context: The cost of a motorway or rail scheme cannot be attributed to one year's sector budget without verified year-by-year allocations. Infrastructure creates services over many years, not just in the construction year.
questions: Is transport spending only road construction?
No. The sector also covers public transport, rail investment, active travel and other responsibilities.
Does higher transport funding mean fares will fall?
No. Fares, subsidies and infrastructure budgets are different choices.
How can a project cost be tracked?
Compare the same project's authorised scope, dated cost estimates, contracts and reported delivery progress.

sectors.short: Debt, EU contributions and other central charges
sectors.intro: Non-voted expenditure is incurred directly from the Exchequer and sits outside the ordinary voted departmental allocations. The site's headline combines debt servicing and EU payments with other central obligations.
sectors.interpretation: It would be incorrect to label the entire €15.6bn as interest on the national debt or as EU membership fees. The category contains distinct non-voted items; look to the Department of Finance for verified components.
sectors.context: Comparisons across years can be affected by the fiscal projections and by the classification of central-fund spending. A detailed breakdown should reconcile against the official non-voted total.
questions: Is all this money interest on government debt?
No. The headline includes EU payments and other non-voted Exchequer items as well as debt-related spending.
What does non-voted expenditure mean?
It refers to spending directly from the central fund under standing authorisations, rather than the usual annual departmental votes.
Does my tax payment go directly to debt interest?
No. Taxes and other revenues are pooled in public funds; the calculator is a proportional illustration, not transaction tracing.

sectors.short: Agriculture, enterprise, defence, higher education and more
sectors.intro: Additional Departments is a collection of multiple public bodies and functions, not one service. It includes activities such as agriculture, enterprise, defence, culture and further and higher education.
sectors.interpretation: The sector's size should not be attributed to any one included department. The official source needs to be mapped at department and programme level before assigning amounts to its constituent themes.
sectors.context: Departmental functions change over time. Housing is presented as a separate sector from 2020, and further and higher education moved away from the schools department in 2020.
questions: Is this a miscellaneous or unexplained spending fund?
No. It is a grouping of identifiable departments and functions, although the headline combines them for presentation.
Why is higher education not simply in Education?
The departments were reorganised in 2020, and the headline categories reflect those accounting boundaries.
Can the themes be assigned euro values?
Only using validated departmental or programme-level source figures. We do not divide the broad total arbitrarily.
